transcript: Solution engineer: What do the inspection reports look like today?
Inspection team lead: Free text. An inspector walks a section, writes what they saw on a tablet, and it lands in a folder. Some are two lines, some are two pages.
Head of track maintenance: We get around three hundred a week across the region. The planners read them on Monday and by Wednesday the urgent ones are found.
Safety assurance lead: Sometimes the urgent ones are found on Friday. That is the problem.
Solution engineer: What should happen instead?
Head of track maintenance: Anything that mentions a defect class we treat as urgent should be at the top of the list the same day, with the sentence that triggered it.
Inspection team lead: The inspectors use their own words. "Wet bed", "pumping", "voiding" all mean roughly the same thing to us.
Solution engineer: Is there an agreed list of urgent defect classes?
Safety assurance lead: There is a standard with categories. I can send it. It is the only list that counts.
Solution engineer: How accurate does the triage need to be?
Safety assurance lead: It must never miss an urgent one. False alarms we can live with.
Head of track maintenance: Within reason. If everything is urgent, nothing is.
Data manager: The reports are in a document store with an API. Some are photos of handwritten notes, maybe one in ten.
Solution engineer: Are those in scope?
Data manager: Not for a first pass. Typed reports only.
Solution engineer: Who would review what the system flags?
Head of track maintenance: The planners, in their Monday session, but daily if the flags are worth it.
Inspection team lead: Please do not change the form the inspectors fill in. Every time someone does, quality drops for months.
Solution engineer: Understood, no change to the input. How will you judge success?
Safety assurance lead: Take last year's reports, run them through, and see whether the ones that became urgent work orders come out on top.
Data manager: We can link reports to work orders for about eighty percent of last year.
Head of track maintenance: If it finds what we already found, faster, that is enough for a pilot.
Solution engineer: Any constraints on where the text goes?
Data manager: Reports contain locations and inspector names. They cannot leave our tenant. Any model has to run inside it or be approved by the data office.
Safety assurance lead: And nothing the system says replaces an inspector's judgement. It is a sorting aid.
Solution engineer: Anything discussed we should leave out?
Head of track maintenance: Predicting where defects will appear. Later, if this works.

traps.note: The standard with urgent categories has not been received.
Whether a model may run outside the tenant needs data office approval.
